sounds.intro: Tajik is a form of Persian, written in Cyrillic with six extra letters. There are no genders and no articles. The stress is usually on the last syllable. Learn the special letters first.
rows: a long "oo" with rounded lips, like German "ö" without the "r"
a "k" made far back in the throat
notes: Tajik is Persian written in Cyrillic, so it shares most words with Persian (Farsi). It has no word order change for questions: the voice goes up.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: Tajik has no gender. "Ӯ" or "вай" means he, she and it. Use "шумо" for one person you respect.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Add -ҳо to the noun (китоб, китобҳо). For people, -он is also used (бача, бачагон). After a number, the noun stays singular: ду китоб (two book).

grammar.title: To be: ҳастам, ҳастӣ, аст
text: "Ҳастам, ҳастӣ, аст, ҳастем, ҳастед, ҳастанд" are the forms of "to be". After a word they shorten: донишҷӯям (I am a student).

grammar.title: Doshtan and hast: have, there is
text: Tajik says "I have" with the verb доштан: дорам, дорӣ, дорад. "Ҳаст" means "there is", "нест" means "there is not".

grammar.title: Present tense: ме-
text: Put ме- before the verb stem and add an ending. Рафтан (to go), stem рав: ме-рав-ам.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: The verb goes last. Order: who, where or when, what, verb. Tajik has no articles: "китоб" means "a book" or "the book".

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put на- before the verb: меравам (I go), намеравам (I do not go). For "to be" use "нест" (is not). "Надорам" means "I do not have". Always compare with the positive form.
ex: ман бо забони англисӣ гап мезанам
man bo zah-bo-nee ahn-glee-SEE gap meh-zah-NAM
ман бо забони англисӣ гап намезанам
man bo zah-bo-nee ahn-glee-SEE gap nah-meh-zah-NAM
I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Say the sentence with a rising voice, or begin with "оё". The word order does not change.
ex: оё шумо бо забони англисӣ гап мезанед?
o-YO shoo-MO bo zah-bo-nee ahn-glee-SEE gap meh-zah-NED

grammar.title: Question words
text: Question words stand where the answer would stand.

grammar.title: Possessives and liking
text: Endings go on the noun: -ам (my), -ат (your), -аш (his / her), -амон (our), -атон (your, formal). To say you like something, use "маъқул аст" (it is pleasing) or "дӯст доштан" (to love).

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: ту (informal): friends, family, children. шумо (formal): strangers, older people, work. Verb endings change: -ӣ (informal), -ед (formal).
rows: аҳволат чӣ хел? / аҳволи шумо чӣ хел?
ah-vo-LAT chee KHEL / ah-vo-lee shoo-MO chee KHEL

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past: the past stem + person ending (рафтам = I went). Future: хоҳам + the short form (хоҳам рафт = I will go).

grammar.title: Commands
text: Informal: бе- + the present stem (биё, come). Formal: add -ед (биёед). To forbid, use на- instead of бе-.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: Can: метавонам + the verb (шино карда метавонам, I can swim). Must: бояд. Want: мехоҳам (бояд and мехоҳам are followed by the short form).
ex: шумо ба ман кӯмак карда метавонед?
shoo-MO bah man koo-MAK kar-DAH meh-tah-vo-NED
I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: Tajik uses little words in front: дар (in, at), ба (to), аз (from), бо (with), барои (for). The "-и" links nouns (izofat): китоби ман (my book).
ex: the book is on the table
the cat is under the table
the shop is next to the bank
the park is near the station
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: Add -тар to the adjective for "more": калон, калонтар. For "the most" add -тарин: калонтарин. "Than" is аз.
